# How the models rank, and what drives their scores

<!-- generated by python/scripts/74_model_drivers.py from committed results; do not edit -->

> **Synthetic charts, scored against the generator's answer key: agreement with it, not clinical accuracy.** Counts of what the committed runs did (`data/datasets/ladder/ladder_preds.csv`), read after the runs: they describe, they do not prove. Generated by `python/scripts/74_model_drivers.py`; tables in `data/datasets/model_drivers/` and, on Databricks, `health_transformation_lab.gold_perio_bench.model_*`.

The same format the agent competition used to compare agents (gemma-developer-agent `docs/findings.md`): a ranked table with paired tests against the leader; pairs of models that differ in one feature, tested the same way; and which facts of a chart, and which features of a model, predict whether a chart is read right, scored by AUC. Every method here reads the chart note alone; the rule phenotypes that read the whole record are on the [full leaderboard](results.md).

## 1. The ranking

**modernbert-large+rules4** reads 203 of 223 charts right. 9 other methods are not distinguishable from it by an exact McNemar test on the same charts (p ≥ 0.05); that is no difference detected, not a tie shown.

- **Rank**: the 95% range of the method's rank among these 43 over paired chart resamples.
- **Leader only / method only**: charts the leader reads right and this method doesn't, and the reverse; the McNemar p is on these two counts.
- **Of the leader-only charts, L3 / stage 4**: where the gap to the leader comes from: notes that leave the diagnosis to be inferred (L3), and stage 4 patients.

Each row pools the pairs of methods that differ in that one feature and nothing else (b is the method with the change). ## 3. What decides whether a chart is read right

Over all 9,589 method-chart runs, a logistic regression predicts correct from the chart's facts, the model's features, or both (out-of-fold AUC, folds and 95% bootstrap by chart):

| Predictors | AUC (95% CI) |
|---|---|
| The chart's facts alone | 0.80 (0.73 to 0.86) |
| The model's features alone | 0.52 (0.49 to 0.55) |
| Both | 0.80 (0.74 to 0.86) |

The chart decides more than the model: model features add almost nothing to the chart facts, because the models differ on a handful of charts (section 1's leader-only columns: L3 notes and stage 4 patients), and an additive fit can't credit a rule that helps only stage 4. Leaving one group of predictors out of the full fit, the AUC lost ranks the drivers:

| Left out | Kind | AUC lost |
|---|---|---:|
| how the note states the diagnosis (L1 2017 terms, L2 older terms, L3 inferred) | chart | 0.196 |
| the true status group | chart | 0.050 |
| how the diagnosis is written | chart | 0.010 |
| the note is copied forward from an earlier visit | chart | 0.002 |
| larger model | model | 0.001 |
| another architecture | model | 0.000 |
| domain pretraining (general to clinical or biomedical) | model | 0.000 |
| another approach | model | 0.000 |
| radiograph features added | model | -0.000 |
| stage 4 rule added | model | -0.000 |
| class weighting | model | -0.000 |
| the note gives measurements | chart | -0.006 |
| note style | chart | -0.008 |
| note length in words | chart | -0.009 |

## Where this lives on Databricks

`python/scripts/75_load_model_drivers.py` (spec 042 US2) loads everything above, and more, into the dev workspace. Loading again replaces the tables and adds no run or trace.

| What | Where | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| The seven tables on this page | `health_transformation_lab.gold_perio_bench.model_rank`, `model_feature`, `model_contrast`, `model_feature_effect`, `chart_feature_effect`, `driver_fit`, `driver_drop` | The same rows as `data/datasets/model_drivers/`, with a comment on every table and column saying what the number means, and the batch key (`run_id`, `run_ts`, `git_commit_sha`) |
| Every method on every chart | `gold_perio_bench.model_chart_result` (43 × 223 rows) | What each method answered, whether it was right, unsafe (could harm if acted on) or the wrong stage, and the chart's facts: one query for "which L3 charts does the leader miss" |
| One MLflow run per method | experiment `/Shared/perio-bench-model-ranking` | Features as params, scores as metrics: the experiment's compare view ranks and filters them |
| One trace per LLM reader call | the same experiment; spans and assessments in `health_transformation_lab.ops_agent_trace.perio_reader_*` | The synthetic note in, the model's answer out, tokens and latency, scored by code scorers: `is_correct`, `is_unsafe_error`, `is_wrong_stage`, `is_gate_ok`, `is_fallback` |

```sql
-- the ranking, with the features that explain it
select rank_position_count, method_code, correct_count, vs_leader_p_ratio, size_code, domain_code, is_rules4
from health_transformation_lab.gold_perio_bench.model_rank order by rank_position_count;

-- the charts the leader misses, and who gets them
select r.visit_id, r.difficulty_code, r.truth_group_code, r.predicted_group_code,
       count_if(o.is_correct) as methods_right_count
from health_transformation_lab.gold_perio_bench.model_chart_result r
join health_transformation_lab.gold_perio_bench.model_chart_result o using (visit_id)
where r.method_code = 'modernbert-large+rules4' and not r.is_correct group by all order by 5 desc;

-- the LLM readers' assessments, per model
select a.name as assessment_code,
       variant_get(s.attributes, '$["gen_ai.request.model"]', 'string') as model_code,
       avg(variant_get(a.value, '$', 'boolean')::int) as true_ratio, count(*) as trace_count
from health_transformation_lab.ops_agent_trace.perio_reader_otel_annotations a
join health_transformation_lab.ops_agent_trace.perio_reader_otel_spans s on s.trace_id = a.target_id
where a.name in ('is_correct', 'is_unsafe_error', 'is_wrong_stage', 'is_gate_ok', 'is_fallback')
group by all order by model_code, assessment_code;
```
